# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Mar 23, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing CircleCI test statistics by mapping flaky test markers to structured statuses. An issue was opened for missing TLS support in proxyd's WebSocket upstreams, and a flaky test related to supernode interop was closed after appearing fixed.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Enhanced CircleCI Test Statistics
A new feature was added to the `cci-stats` service to improve the reporting of flaky tests. This update introduces a helper function to detect `FLAKY_FAIL:` and `FLAKY_PASS:` prefixes in CircleCI test skip messages, allowing these tests to be passed through with structured statuses instead of being filtered out. This provides more granular insight into test suite stability. ([#576](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/576))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Resolution of Flaky Supernode Interop Test
The `TestSupernodeSameTimestampInvalidTransitive` flaky test was closed today. After an analysis of 500 pipelines on `develop`, the test has not failed in the last 43 consecutive runs, indicating it is likely fixed. ([#19570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19570))

## NEW ISSUES

### Proxyd WebSocket TLS Support
A new issue was opened to address the lack of TLS support for WebSocket upstreams in `proxyd`. Currently, backend TLS client certificates are only applied to HTTP upstreams, leaving WebSocket connections without this security feature. ([#577](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/577))

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Kona Guest Panics Deserializing `chainList.json` ([#19654](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19654))
A new comment today saved a Notion link related to the kona guest panicking when deserializing the superchain registry chain list, specifically due to a missing `name` field. This issue was observed during `TestChallengerPlaysGame`.

### Flaky Test: `TestCLELDivergence` ([#19681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19681))
Discussion continues on this flaky test. The latest comment from today suggests investigating the reason for a `Deriver system is resetting` warning, which is an `ErrEngineResetReq`. It was noted that this reset is expected during normal startup and initial pipeline initialization, not necessarily an issue during EL sync. The assessment is that the test comment is incorrect regarding the source of the reset, and there is no reset bug.

### Interop Phase 3: Removing Chains From Shared Dispute Games ([#19692](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19692))
A comment today clarified that this issue refers to supporting the removal of chains from the interop set within the proofs system, not solving all interop-related problems. An earlier comment questioned the necessity and implications of removing chains from the interop set.

### CGT Chains and Shared Dispute Games ([#19711](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19711))
A comment today highlighted a potential issue from a design document, noting that enabling the correct predeploys in the interop fork for Custom Gas Token (CGT) chains requires a workaround, specifically not deploying or enabling the current `SuperchainETHBridge`/`ETHLiquidity` contracts.

### [tracking]: Review `kona-interop` block hash oracle ([#18288](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18288))
An update today detailed the progress on adding a fixture-based integration test for `OracleInteropProvider::header_by_number` in `kona-proof-interop`. A full acceptance test was deemed impractical due to its long runtime. The new approach uses real OP Mainnet state/storage trie proof data to build an in-memory mock oracle, forcing the production path for EIP-2935 history lookup and header resolution, running significantly faster. The old action test can be removed once this new test merges.

### Consider overlap between CGT and ETHLiquidity contracts ([#19461](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19461))
A comment today noted that the overlap between CGT and ETHLiquidity contracts is worthy of consideration as part of scoping the case for CGT chains joining interop.
